objective: Build the two detectors that make record staleness findable instead of accidental: a two-timestamp sweep that flags any record whose case evidence moved after the record last did, and a reconciliation stamp plus commit-time check that flags a record asserting a verdict its author never reconciled against the case history, which is the failure mode the two-timestamp sweep provably cannot see
rationale: The lab amends stale records well and finds them badly. Measured over tracked markdown on 2026-08-10 there are 36 supersession markers across 27 files and 35 of the 36 carry a date, which is 97 percent compliance with the amend-in-place convention, so the convention is not the gap. Every one of those 36 exists because somebody already knew the record was stale. Nothing in the lab finds the ones nobody noticed, and the record of the one case that was found says it was found by luck: a zero-compute audit whose first act happened to be reading the case's full commit history. The incident behind L-39 is the specimen and it is instructive in a way the lesson does not spell out. Commit fe121af2 of 2026-07-31 archived the sign convention control run that killed the F5c 4 to 12 times premise, and the chief's negative verdict review first committed at 9d72e197 on 2026-08-07 carried that premise as an open mystery and proposed diagnostics for it. The obvious detector, comparing when a record last moved against when its evidence last moved, would NOT have fired here: the refuting commit predates the record by seven days, so the record is newer than its evidence and passes. The review was born stale rather than aged into staleness, and the two failure modes need two instruments. That distinction is the whole content of this proposal and it was found by testing the obvious design against the real incident rather than reasoning about it. Both instruments are pure git over paths already on disk. The case identifier to directory mapping the sweep needs is already mechanical throughout the campaign directory, where F5c resolves to F5c_runs and F5C_ prefixed records, DMR to DMR_runs, B52_RUNG6_REPLICATE to its own runs directory, so no new metadata is required for detector A at all. Detector B adds one line to a record and per L-46 the artifact was audited from both ends before proposing it: its only consumer is the sweep script itself, no existing check has a passing condition its presence could satisfy because no check parses record front matter, and it introduces no file into any directory that a glob based consumer scans, so it disables nothing and confuses nothing. Axis A: a report kind item at zero solver cost, so it ranks at the ranking floor. Axis B: 0, no wall row moves. Axis C: 0, no scored column is touched.

cost_basis: measured; both detectors are git log reads over paths already on disk, no case is opened and no solver runs, so the cost is text sweep time only
expected_knowledge_gain: Three distinguishable outcomes, each with an action attached. One: detector A fires on a small named set, in which case the lab gains a burn down list and the four known instances in the memory architecture duplicate register are confirmed as the bulk of the problem. Two: detector A fires on a large fraction of the corpus, which means the case identifier to evidence mapping is too coarse rather than that the corpus is rotten, and the finding is a mapping repair before any record is touched, stated as such rather than as a staleness epidemic. Three: detector B, run retrospectively against the specimen, either reproduces the L-39 catch or does not, and that is the load bearing test of the whole proposal because a detector that cannot re-find the one instance the lab already knows about has not been shown to work at all.
sequencing: Dispatchable now. Zero solver cost, competes for no compute with any live campaign, and detector B's commit time check should land before detector A's standing sweep because the write time failure is the one with a proven instance.
gate: PROOF CLAUSE, verbatim. (a) Detector B is run retrospectively against the specimen and MUST flag the 2026-08-07 negative verdict review as asserting an F5c verdict unreconciled against fe121af2; if it does not, the proposal has failed regardless of what else it finds and no further work is done on it. (b) Detector A is run over the full campaign record set and its output is dispositioned row by row into three buckets, genuinely stale, mapping artefact, and already amended, with counts stated; a run that reports a flag rate above 50 percent is reported as a mapping defect and not as a staleness finding. (c) Both detectors report a null as a claim about their own reach, naming which records carried no resolvable case identifier and were therefore never examined, because a sweep that cannot see a record has not cleared it. (d) No record is edited by this work: the output is a list, and every amendment it implies is made by that record's owner under the dated in place convention.
